subject: Secure hosting qualification & next steps (Private / VPC) - Midvale Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@midvalehealth.com>; it-security@midvalehealth.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: secure hosting qualification & next steps

Hi Daniel / Midvale team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured your requirements correctly and to outline the proposed next steps. If anything below is off, please flag and we’ll update.

Key pain points you described
- Current vendor causes inconsistent latency during peak hours; strict SLA expectations for scheduling and telehealth workflows.
- Regulatory obligation to keep PHI within US-only infrastructure and to have customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption.
- Tight network isolation requirements: no outbound internet from the inference cluster, only specific egress via a constrained NAT/proxy controlled by Midvale.

Current stack & constraints you shared
- Core EHR + message bus hosted in AWS us-east-1; procurement prefers to keep inference inside the same VPC or a peered VPC.
- Identity: Okta SSO for users and SCIM for groups.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II in review; annual pentest required before production roll-out.

Success criteria for an initial POC
- Run a 2-node private VPC deployment in us-east-1 with customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and no public IPs.
- Demonstrate < 200ms 95th percentile latency on a baseline 512-token workload for typical telehealth prompts.
- Show audit logs (deploy & inference) forwarded to your SIEM.

Clarifying technical requirements (items for confirmation)
- KMS: You said BYOK via AWS KMS with a CMK in your account — confirm alias/ARN once available.
- Network: We will need a small list of CIDRs and firewall rules (outbound egress only to the endpoints we specify). Can you confirm if you require a bastion/jump host for any deployment admin access?
- Air-gapped/offline option: You mentioned an air-gap for DR — is that an absolute requirement for production, or just a potential option for an isolated environment?

Proposed next steps and owners
1) Midvale: share target CIDRs, KMS key ARN, and contact for networking (Daniel) — due Wed 2026-07-22.
2) Redwood (Olga): send VPC checklist + sample network diagram and a draft POC runbook — sent with this email.
3) Redwood (Vanessa): scope Dedicated capacity and a POC cost estimate for the 2-node private deployment — target 2026-07-23.
4) Joint: 30-min follow-up technical alignment call (network + KMS) — propose Thu 2026-07-23 10:00am ET.

Attachments included: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram-template.png. I’ve also attached a summary of typical procurement steps we’ve seen with similar healthcare customers.

If that timeline looks reasonable, I’ll lock the follow-up call.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: secure hosting qualification & next steps

Olga — thanks for the recap and for the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side:

Corrections/confirmations
- KMS: confirmed — we will provide an AWS KMS CMK ARN (customer in control) for the POC.
- Air-gap: at this stage, air-gapped (fully offline) environments are not mandatory for production. It is a possible DR requirement; please include options and delta effort for an air-gap in the runbook.
- Bastion: yes, our security team requires a bastion host for admin access. No direct SSH from the public internet.

Procurement & timeline notes
- We will need a draft SOW and an initial quote to start internal procurement. Legal review typically takes 2–3 weeks once we have an SOW.
- For the POC, we can greenlight a 6-week technical POC after procurement approval.

Network info we’ll send by Wed 2026-07-22
- CIDR ranges for peered VPC and the egress proxy IPs.
- Firewall rules for allowed egress endpoints.

One ask: Can you include a minimum-latency SLA target and an expected token throughput estimate for the POC in the runbook? That will help our infra team size the instance types appropriately.

I’m available for the alignment call Thu 10am ET. Please go ahead and schedule.

Thanks,
Daniel Kim
Head of IT Security | Midvale Health
daniel.kim@midvalehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Team — forwarding the Midvale responses. Highlights and proposed internal split:

Highlights
- BYOK AWS KMS CMK confirmed for POC.
- Bastion host required; no direct public SSH.
- Air-gap option is a possible DR path (not blocking for initial POC).
- Procurement wants SOW + quote before legal review.

Action items (owners)
- Vanessa: please prepare an initial POC pricing card (2-node private VPC in us-east-1) and a Dedicated capacity delta (monthly) if they want sustained throughput. Include estimated instance types, token throughput, and a nominal latency expectation at 95th percentile. (Due: 2026-07-23)
- Vivek: build a short POC runbook (2–4 pages) that covers: network reqs (CIDRs/firewall), KMS + BYOK steps, bastion access model, logging/audit export to SIEM, and rollback/fallback to hosted model. Add a one-paragraph note on air-gap delta effort. (Due: 2026-07-23)
- Olga: draft SOW template and send an initial quote + sample SOW to Daniel (target 2026-07-22 end of day).

I attached the VPC checklist and a network diagram template to the external thread; I’ll add the draft SOW and the internal cost assumptions in our shared drive link.

Proposed POC timeline (subject to procurement)
- Week 0: SOW/quote signoff
- Week 1–2: infra provisioning & KMS setup (Redwood + Midvale keys)
- Week 3: validation tests and SIEM integration
- Weeks 4–6: performance evaluation and final handoff

Let me know if you want me to pick a time for a quick internal sync before the Thu call.

Thanks —
